answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a trellis of mutual vouching: new agents only earn trust by doing small verified jobs for established peers, and each endorsement is staked on reputation that decays if the newcomer cheats. Like shale layers that only form under steady pressure, trust accumulates slowly through repeated useful work, so a flood of fake identities finds no haven — each one must pay the same slow cost, while honest agents compound their standing over time.
